description.narrative: 2021-2023 1.1 Feasibility study completed identifying the essential areas, which the project activities will concentrate on during its implementation. 1.2 Number of government officials, executives, experts, and policy makers of central and local government agencies, etc attending regional conference to discuss findings of the feasibility study and decide on the topics the project will concentrate on with the participation of ACSH P2P Alliances on innovation, digitalisation, and e-governance members among others 1.3 Number of government officials, executives, experts, and policy makers of central and local government agencies, etc attending seminars introducing the concept of innovation and its potential uses in government and governance practices and in utilising differentiated channels of public service delivery through digitalisation – including the Korean experience. 1.4 Number of government officials, executives, experts, and policy makers of central and local government agencies, etc attending workshops that elaborate on policy design to create an environment conducive to innovative practices, as well as uses of innovative practices employed by the Government of Korea. 1.5 Number of methodological guides produced on how to introduce innovative practices in government and on what steps to follow in digitalising public services. 1.6 Number of knowledge products prepared and published on methodologies to introduce innovation in government and case studies of successful implementation of innovation practices in government and introducing differentiated channels of public service delivery through digitalisation of public services. 2.1 Number of government officials, executives, experts, and policy makers of central and local government agencies, etc. exposed to innovation practices in governance and the provision of public services through differentiated channels of delivery through study tours to witness the Korean experience.

comment.narrative:
1.1 Feasibility study completed identifying the essential areas, which the project activities will concentrate on during its implementation -1; The final report of the study was completed at the end of February 2022. It was shared with the government entities and other organisations that are directly involved with digitalisation policy and implementation in the seven countries participating in this project. Dissemination of the final report had a dual purpose, one to inform participants of the current situation in digitalisation transformation in the seven participating countries, and two for them to contemplate on the topics that they would like capacity building activities to be organised in the remaining part of 2022 and for 2023. Drawing on the findings of the feasibility study, ACSH experts developed a research paper titled “Digitalisation of Public Service Delivery, and Innovation in Government Operations in Central Asia and the Caucasus” and submitted for publication to the International Journal of Civil Service Reform and Practice.
1.2 Number of government officials, executives, experts, and policy makers of central and local government agencies, etc attending regional conference to discuss findings of the feasibility study and decide on the topics the project will concentrate on with the participation of ACSH P2P Alliances on innovation, digitalisation, and e-governance members among others - 50; The regional conference aimed at discussing the findings of the needs-assessment study – that was postponed in 2021 due to the pandemic-induced travel restrictions – took place in Astana, Kazakhstan on 14 April 2022. Following the presentation of the needs-assessment study findings, the participants discussed such findings and confirmed the planned activities’ scope and content for the remaining part of 2022. The number of direct beneficiaries from the seven participating countries was 50 individuals of which 17 were female (34%) and 33 male (66%).
1.3 Number of government officials, executives, experts, and policy makers of central and local government agencies, etc attending seminars introducing the concept of innovation and its potential uses in government and governance practices and in utilising differentiated channels of public service delivery through digitalisation – including the Korean experience -50;. 1.4 Number of government officials, executives, experts, and policy makers of central and local government agencies, etc attending workshops that elaborate on policy design to create an environment conducive to innovative practices, as well as uses of innovative practices employed by the Government of Korea -100.
Overall, three seminar-workshops have been organised focused on Cooperation and Capacity Development in Digital Government, Digital Government Policy Frameworks and Open data policies, practices and cases. The number of direct beneficiaries from the seven participating countries was 136, including 84 male (62%) and 38 female (38%).
1.5 Number of methodological guides produced on how to introduce innovative practices in government and on what steps to follow in digitalising public services -0; It was postponed to 2023 in agreement with implementing partners.
1.6 Number of knowledge products prepared and published on methodologies to introduce innovation in government and case studies of successful implementation of innovation practices in government and introducing differentiated channels of public service delivery through digitalisation of public services -1;
A knowledge product based on the comparative analysis on open data policies and practices has been prepared and disseminated among the participating countries of this project and beyond.
2.1 Number of government officials, executives, experts, and policy makers of central and local government agencies, etc. exposed to innovation practices in governance and the provision of public services through differentiated channels of delivery through study tours to witness the Korean experience -20.
A study visit to the Republic of Korea was organised for representatives of the seven participating countries between 19 and 21 September to observe first-hand “public service delivery utilising state-of-the-art digital technologies”. The study visit provided an opportunity for participants to familiarise themselves with Korea’s knowledge and experience in public service innovation and emerging technologies, and to identify ways and means that may also be applicable for the project’s participating countries. The number of direct beneficiaries from the seven participating countries was 20, including 15 male (75%) and 5 female (25%).
